Run a pre-planned analysis from an instrument's analysis plan

Source: R/analysis_plan.R
run_analysis_plan.Rd

Executes every analysis block defined in the instrument's analysis_plan slot against the supplied response data. Each block corresponds to one research question defined during instrument design in the SurveyBuilder. Results include APA-formatted statistics, effect sizes, interpretation prompts and reporting references.

Usage

run_analysis_plan(
  data,
  instrument,
  scored = TRUE,
  plots = FALSE,
  plot_palette = c("web", "print"),
  seed = 20260828L,
  strict = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

A tibble or data.frame of responses, typically produced by read_responses() or read_sheet_responses().

instrument

An sframe object containing an analysis_plan.

scored

Logical. Whether to automatically score scales before running the analysis. Defaults to TRUE.

plots

Logical. When TRUE and ggplot2 is installed, supported blocks gain a $plot element holding a brand-styled ggplot object: bar charts for frequency and chi-square blocks, scatter plots with a regression overlay for correlation and linear-regression blocks. Defaults to FALSE.

plot_palette

One of "web" (brand colours, for on-screen use) or "print" (black, grey and white, for journal-ready print figures). Applied to every plot attached when plots = TRUE. See theme_surveyframe().

seed

Integer or NULL. The random seed the analysis runs under. Defaults to a fixed value so the same instrument and the same data give the same answer every time, which is what makes a rendered report usable as an audit artefact. Every bootstrap confidence interval in the plan, and the parallel analysis behind the EFA family, depend on it. Pass NULL for the unseeded behaviour of releases before 0.4.1. Each block's stream starts from this seed and the block's id, so a block gives the same interval whatever blocks come before it. The caller's own random stream is restored afterwards, so seeding here does not affect anything that runs later.

strict

Logical. When TRUE, an error is raised if any block fails or scale scoring fails, listing each failure. When FALSE, the default, failures are kept in the results and counted in their status.

Value

An object of class sframe_analysis_results, a list with one element per analysis block, named by block id. Its status attribute holds blocks, succeeded, failed, failed_blocks and scoring, the outcome of scoring scales before analysis. A normal return can hold failed blocks, so check attr(results, "status")$failed or use strict = TRUE. Each element contains the test result, APA string, interpretation prompt and reporting-reference metadata. Inferential blocks also carry a $table data frame suitable for knitr::kable(). Pass to render_results() to generate a formatted report.

Cross-tabulations

A crosstab or chi_square block's result carries $totals, the counts with a Total row and column. Set options = list(percent = "row"), "column" or "total" for $percent_table, the percentages over that denominator. The Total row of row percentages is the column distribution, and the Total column of column percentages is the row distribution. The report then shows each count with its percentage beside it, and the chart draws the percentages.

Weights

A frequency, descriptives, cross-tabulation or chi-square block may name a case-weight column in its weights role. The researcher sets a design weight, so it may be a column that is not an item: validate_sframe() notes it, and it must then be in the responses, read with read_responses(meta_cols = ). A block whose weight column is missing, or holds a negative, non-finite or non-numeric value, fails with a message saying so.

How answers are coded

Categories follow 1 order in every locale: the codes of the item's choice set as the instrument declares them, then factor levels, then any other value, numbers by value and other text in code point order. A category nobody chose is dropped before a model is fitted.

  • McNemar's test lays both items out on that order, so each category is paired with itself. 2 items with different choice sets are refused.

  • An ordinal logistic outcome is ordered as its choice set declares. The result's $outcome_levels and its sentence give the order.

  • In every model (linear, binary, ordinal, multinomial and Firth logistic regression, and the ANCOVA covariates) a single_choice or multiple_choice item enters as a category, with 1 indicator term per category after the first, whatever its codes look like. The first category with answers is the reference. The result's $predictor_coding lists each categorical predictor's levels, and the sentence names each reference category.

  • A binary or Firth logistic model gives the odds of its event, the last category of its outcome in that order (1 of 0 and 1, the last declared code of a choice set). options = list(event = "yes") names another. The result's $event and $reference_level, and its sentence, name both. A multinomial model's reference is the first category.

See also

render_results(), read_sheet_responses()

Other Analyse functions: score_scales(), sframe_assumption_results(), sframe_descriptives_results(), sframe_efa_readiness_results(), sframe_efa_solution(), sframe_item_results(), sframe_posthoc_results(), sframe_reliability_results(), sframe_validity_results()

Examples

instr <- read_sframe(
  system.file("extdata", "demos", "two_group.sframe",
              package = "surveyframe")
)
responses <- read_responses(
  system.file("extdata", "demos", "two_group_responses.csv",
              package = "surveyframe"),
  instr,
  respondent_id = "respondent_id",
  submitted_at = "submitted_at",
  meta_cols = "started_at"
)
# \donttest{
results <- run_analysis_plan(responses, instr)
print(results)
# }
